content:
Hi everyone,

I'm proud to announce a project I've been working on for the past few months: https://github.com/Rob23oba/dependent-computability, a framework for automatically proving computability. Using this project, you can prove that any function that only depends on propext and Quot.sound (and no nested or reflexive inductives) is computable (unless there are bugs in the code lol). As a simple example of what it's capable of:

import DependentComputability

def test (x : Nat) : Nat :=
  (((x / (x + 3) : Rat) * 30) ^ 2 - 27).floor.toNat

set_option Elab.async false in
lemma test_computable : Computable test := by
  have_new hcomp : DComp test := by
    dcomp_tac
  exact hcomp_extra.computable (new% test)

Note that none of the operations here have special support; computability theorems for Rat.floor and Int.toNat and Rat addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and powers are generated on the fly.

Limitations

  1. The most common cause of failure is that a proof uses Classical.choice; I'll work on reducing the number of cases where this happens. The only cases where this is really unavoidable are when a proof requires choice and works with type equality (or really just a proposition without any restrictions).
  2. Again, nested and reflexive inductives don't work automatically. However, if you really wanted to, you could always write the basic definitions and lemmas for them manually and then rely on the automation to do the rest. This has been partly done for Lean.Syntax to make autoParams work.
  3. This project uses the toolchain leanprover/lean4-pr-releases:pr-release-8867-9a8a69e! This means that if you have another dependency except Mathlib, you'll might run into problems. The reason why I don't use an official toolchain is that I need Sort (imax u u v) = Sort (imax u v) as a defeq.
  4. While everything else should work in principle, in practice, it can get quite slow. I'll continue working on improving performance for generating computability proofs.
